name: Generative ambient pad from a MIDI FX chain: chord → arp → random → scale-quantize last, uneven loop lengths, send-return FX as blendable layers, slow LFOs on send/filter/gain
goal: Build a long, non-looping ambient pad from one held note by chaining portable MIDI processors (chord generator → arpeggiator → random pitch → scale quantizer LAST), layering octave/texture ranges, stacking uneven loop lengths (5/7/18 bars) so repeats never line up, routing FX sends back to audio tracks as blendable layers, and driving send amount / HPF / tone / gain with slow free-running LFOs. Delta vs generative-ambient-drones (clip-pool chance, seed-random MIDI clip, noise-wind, random-modulators): this is a live MIDI-effect chain with scale-quantize forced at the end and probability-weighted scale degrees (root/fifth-heavy), plus uneven multi-bar loops and send-return FX treated as instruments.

source.title: Making INFINITE Ambient Pads Like The 1975 (Ableton Sound Design Tutorial)

prerequisites: Any DAW with MIDI FX or equivalent (chord/interval generator, arpeggiator, random/chance pitch, scale quantizer) and send/return routing
One or more tonal sources (felt piano, soft guitar, synth pad) covering distinct octave/texture ranges
At least one free-running LFO / macro modulator that can map to send level, filter cutoff, and gain

inputs.name: held_root_or_sparse_notes
inputs.description: One held note or sparse MIDI that the MIDI FX chain expands

inputs.name: key_and_scale
inputs.description: Target key/scale for the final quantizer (e.g. C major pentatonic, or root+fifth-only for cleaner pads)

outputs.name: generative_ambient_pad_bed
outputs.description: Long unique pad stem (render or live) that does not hard-loop every 4 bars

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate with stock MIDI FX / Web Audio / any DAW; no proprietary presets, banks, or sample packs copied.
Scale quantizer MUST be last in the MIDI chain so random/arp notes cannot leave the chosen scale.
Prefer root/fifth-heavy degree maps for clean pads; open seconds only at low probability.
Uneven loop lengths (e.g. 5, 7, 18 bars) across layers — avoid identical 4-bar stacks that phase as a loop.
Steady pitch preference: keep any pitch-shift LFO depth tiny and gated by a slower depth LFO (flutter in/out), not constant random vib.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, enter by about count 8; pad-only before that.

steps.action: Pick sources by texture and octave: e.g. dusty mid felt/piano for midrange, brighter guitar or glass for highs, optional soft bass for lows. Plan the pad like a mini arrangement so layers occupy different ranges.
steps.expect: Distinct mid / high / low textures ready

steps.action: Build the MIDI FX chain on a MIDI track feeding the mid source: (1) chord/interval generator (e.g. major-7 from a single held note), (2) arpeggiator (rate/gate sets the pad 'timbre' of motion), (3) random/chance pitch module, (4) scale quantizer LAST locked to key/scale.
steps.expect: One held note becomes scale-safe generative arpeggiated chords

steps.action: Bias the scale map toward root and fifth for cleaner pads (example probabilities from source: ~1/3 low root, ~1/6 high octave root, ~5/12 fifth, ~1/12 major second). Raise random chance toward 100% for freer pads, or lower it to stay closer to played notes.
steps.expect: Most notes land on root/fifth; sparseness controllable

steps.action: Record or clip several generative passes at uneven lengths (5-bar, 7-bar, ~18-bar) on different layers/textures. Multiply them out so overlaps are intentional and never a clean 4-bar stack.
steps.expect: Layers fade in/out of each other without a hard loop feel

steps.action: Route interesting FX (granular octave-up, cloud/plate reverb, creative delay) via sends that return to dedicated audio tracks — treat each return as a blendable instrument, optionally re-send into a shared room reverb. Optional: send a return back into itself for controlled feedback.
steps.expect: FX beds sit as mixable tracks, not just master glue

steps.action: Map slow free-running LFOs to: send amount into the octave-up/granular return (with a non-zero floor so it never fully disappears), high-pass cutoff, source tone/color macros, and a utility gain on the bass layer (~0–50% depth) so low end breathes in and out over long stretches. Offset LFO phases so moves duck past each other. Optional nested LFO: one LFO modulates pitch-shift depth of a reverb send (0%→tiny %) for intermittent flutter.
steps.expect: Small, gradual dynamics over many bars; no abrupt on/off

steps.action: Render a long unique stem (or save the rack/template). Swap source instrument, reverb flavor, or scale (e.g. major vs major-pentatonic) to mint new pads from the same chain.
steps.expect: Reusable generative pad template + unique audio

verification: Holding one note produces continuous scale-locked motion with no out-of-key spikes (quantizer last).
Multi-layer playback does not feel like a locked 4-bar loop (uneven lengths audible).
Send returns appear as blendable tracks; slow LFOs change send/filter/gain gradually.
Bass utility LFO creates long sections with and without low end.
